description: Import up to 100000 rows into a data model as a background job. Use it instead of import_records for more than 1000 rows. The rows are uploaded, then validated - nothing is written while any row is still unchecked - and the valid rows are written in batches. Returns the job at once: follow it with get_record_import until status is awaitingConfirmation, completed, failed or cancelled. With onInvalid STOP (the default) a job with invalid rows stops at awaitingConfirmation: read them with list_record_import_rows (status invalid), then confirm_record_import to write the valid rows or cancel_record_import to write none. A row over 65536 bytes is staged as invalid. A model runs one import at a time: a start while another is running is refused and the uploaded rows are discarded - read the running one with get_record_import by modelIdOrSlug.

onInvalid.description: What happens when validation refuses a row. STOP (the default) writes nothing and leaves the job awaitingConfirmation until confirm_record_import or cancel_record_import; CONTINUE writes the valid rows without asking.

rows.description: Array of plain objects keyed by the model's field keys, in the same shape import_records takes: a translatable field takes a language map ({ title: { en: '...', no: '...' } }). Row numbers in the job are positions in this array, starting at 1.

upsertKey.description: A key from the model's uniqueFields, or its product skuField. A row whose value matches an existing record updates that record; any other row is created. Not allowed on member (auth) models.

name: start_record_import
title: Start record import
